rationale: Coverage: The review fully addresses all required points: what can be done in simulation, what requires real data, how to reduce real-robot training/screening overhead, comparison of three evidence types, and why simulation success or transfer metric correlation cannot replace real-robot validation. It also explicitly notes limitations and scope. Factuality: All claims are supported by the provided abstracts; the review carefully distinguishes abstract-level evidence and avoids overgeneralization. It correctly notes that 1809.08626v3 is not about policy transfer and uses it only as a boundary case. Citation support: Each cited paper is used appropriately; [2009.12864v1] supports transfer metric and correlation claims, [1809.10253v3] supports skill composition and real-robot validation, and [1809.08626v3] is correctly cited for domain adaptation in predictive maintenance. No unsupported or mismatched citations found. Consistency: The review maintains consistent terminology and logical flow; it clearly separates evidence types and does not contradict itself. The conclusion aligns with the earlier analysis.
